Nyirlugos Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírlugos, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírlugos's Jewish community, settled from the first half of the 18th century, joined the Orthodox stream following the 1869 Jewish Congress. Around 1900, its rabbi was Eliezer Meir Lazrus Schiffmann, described as one of the greatest sages of his era and among the last students of the renowned Gaon Rabbi Shmuel Shmelke Klein of Nagyszőlős; Schiffmann later became head of a local yeshiva after 20 years as a merchant. In 1944, the village's 136 Jews were confined in the synagogue, then transported via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto and a farm called Hargond to Auschwitz; none survived the death camps. This cemetery was established as early as 1870, per that year's cadastral map.
